article_title: The Price of Finding a Certificate: Unsupported Pareto Points under Prefix Queries
article_abstract: We study the cost of discovering a certificate for a designated candidate whose two objectives are means of ordered vector records. Each query purchases the next whole record of one configuration. Algorithms must decide correctly on every legal archive; their acquisition cost on positive archives is compared with the cheapest realised prefix proving both Pareto nondomination and unsupportedness under nonzero nonnegative weights. When the cost coordinate is unbounded, we determine the exact deterministic and zero-error randomised ratios for every catalogue size and archive length. The randomised lower bound covers numerical policies and arbitrary prefix interleavings through a causal Ramsey reduction. Bounded diagonal bands yield sharp three-configuration transitions under positive row prices. For three configurations on the triangle, a mixed acquisition policy has ratio at most 87/80. This strictly improves on the exact asymptotic ratio 12/11 for policies that fully observe the candidate before TRUE, establishing a separation between the policy classes. The unrestricted asymptotic lower bound remains 23/22. A certificate-preservation criterion characterises transcript-preserving policy transfer, and public constant blocks yield sharp comparator-distortion bounds. Supplementary results give a faster retrospective comparator, higher-dimensional certificates and a margin-based disclosure guarantee. For three alternatives, arbitrary-dimensional unsupportedness reduces to scalar interval feasibility; a public two-anchor row representation also preserves paid-prefix costs. The unrestricted triangle optimum and convergence of its optimal-ratio sequence remain open.
